title: Duplicate charges and repeated payments
overview: Two similar entries can represent duplicate completed payments, a pending authorization plus a posted payment, or separate transactions. Compare their status, date, amount and merchant description before concluding that both are final debits.
procedure: The synthetic dispute workflow records the non-sensitive details and checks fictional transaction status after verification. A demo agent reviews the alleged duplicate; a refund is not guaranteed and no real chargeback is submitted by this assistant.

title: Failed or debited-but-unsuccessful payments
overview: A failed payment can leave no debit, a pending debit or an entry later reversed. Determine the channel and final displayed status before retrying, since repeated attempts can create additional authorizations or duplicate payments.
procedure: For the demo, describe whether the attempt used a card, UPI or a bank transfer and whether money was debited. An agent can review the synthetic entry and relevant procedure; the assistant does not promise automatic reversal within an invented timeframe.

title: Refunds not received and merchant disputes
overview: A merchant refund is separate from the original purchase and can have its own processing reference. A cancellation notice alone may not show that a refund has reached the account; the merchant and bank records may need to be compared.
procedure: Keep the merchant confirmation and non-sensitive dates for the synthetic review. After verification, inspect the fictional credit entry and ask an agent to reconcile an unresolved refund; no fixed credit date or entitlement is invented.

title: Chargebacks and card disputes
overview: A chargeback is a dispute mechanism used under applicable card-network and issuer processes. It is not the same as a merchant voluntarily refunding a payment and does not guarantee that a disputed amount will be returned.
procedure: The demo agent asks for a non-sensitive description, relevant dates and steps already taken with the merchant. Actual eligibility, evidence and deadlines must come from the issuer's rules; the assistant does not provide legal advice or file a real dispute.

title: Complaints and human support
overview: A complaint records an unresolved service issue for review. A support agent can help distinguish a transaction dispute from a general service complaint and explain the institution's tracking process. Keep the issue timeline and any earlier support references so the reviewer can avoid repeating completed checks.
procedure: The Call Sense Bank demo creates a human handoff with the masked conversation and an issue summary. Ask for the case reference and next review step; this simulation does not submit a complaint to a real institution or regulator.

title: Complaint references and follow-up
overview: A complaint reference identifies a case, while its current status describes the review stage. Acknowledgement does not necessarily mean the underlying problem is resolved; additional information may be needed.
procedure: For a synthetic case, use the agent queue to inspect Open, Needs Follow-up, Escalated Further or Resolved status. Only permitted non-sensitive information should be added; real escalation deadlines must be confirmed with the responsible institution.
